# `slopmax`

Pool your Claude, ChatGPT, and SuperGrok subscriptions behind one local proxy, so Claude Code, Codex, and Grok Build keep working when an account runs out.

Run without a command to see your accounts, or to set slopmax up the first time.


## Examples

**Set everything up, step by step**

```
slopmax setup
```

**Add another Claude account**

```
slopmax login claude
```

**Run Codex through the proxy**

```
slopmax run codex
```

**Read the accounts' standing as JSON**

```
slopmax status --json
```

- **Usage:** `slopmax [SUBCOMMAND]`

## Flags
- **`-h --help`** — Print help
- **`-V --version`** — Print version

## Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | it worked |
| `1` | it failed; the error says why |
| `2` | the command line was wrong |

## `slopmax setup`

- **Usage:** `slopmax setup [FLAGS]`
- **Aliases:** `init`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Set slopmax up step by step, or unattended with flags.

It finds the logins Claude Code, Codex, and CLIProxyAPI hold and offers to bring them over, signs in to more accounts, picks how accounts are shared, points your agents at the proxy, and starts it at login. Every question has a flag; with --yes, or without a terminal, it asks nothing and takes the flags, else the recommended answers.

With --hub, this machine uses the slopmax on another of your machines instead, and runs no proxy of its own.

### Flags
- **`-y --yes`** — Ask nothing: take the flags, else the recommended answers
- **`--import <SOURCES>`** — Take logins from these tools

  **Choices:** `all`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `cliproxyapi`, `none`
- **`--adopt`** — With --import cliproxyapi: refresh its logins here instead of following its files
- **`--login <PROVIDERS>`** — Sign in to these subscriptions

  **Choices:** `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, `none`
- **`--keys-from-env`** — Add the keys set in ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, and XAI_API_KEY
- **`--strategy <STRATEGY>`** — How new sessions pick an account

  **Choices:** `reset-first`, `fill-first`, `least-used`, `round-robin`
- **`--affinity <AFFINITY>`** — Keep each session on its account (on), or place every request afresh (off)

  **Choices:** `on`, `off`
- **`--agents <AGENTS>`** — Point these agents at the proxy

  **Choices:** `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, `none`
- **`--no-service`** — Don't start slopmax at login
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

### Using a hub
- **`--hub <HUB>`** — Use the slopmax on another of your machines: its name, host[:port], or URL; `off` goes back
- **`--find-hub`** — Look for slopmax on your tailnet, and use it
- **`--hub-key <KEY>`** — A key the hub made for this machine (else $SLOPMAX_HUB_KEY)
- **`--key-name <NAME>`** — With the hub's owner key: the name of the key made for this machine

### Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | it worked |
| `1` | it failed; the error says why |
| `2` | the command line was wrong |

### Examples

**Unattended, for a script or an agent**

```
slopmax setup --yes --import claude-code,codex --agents claude,codex
```

**Use the slopmax on another of your machines**

```
slopmax setup --hub workstation
```

**Go back to this machine's own proxy**

```
slopmax setup --hub off
```

## `slopmax status`

- **Usage:** `slopmax status [FLAGS]`
- **Effect:** read-only

Show the accounts, their usage windows, and when limits reset.

Reads the running proxy, else the files on disk. Accounts are numbered; commands that take <ACCOUNT> take those numbers.

### Flags
- **`-r --refresh`** — Fetch fresh usage from the providers first
- **`-w --watch`** — Keep the display up to date until interrupted
- **`--json`** — Print JSON instead of text, for scripts and agents
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

### Output Formats

- **`human`** (default)

  **Framing:** `text`
- **`json`**

  **Framing:** `json`; **Select:** `--json`

  **Media type:** `application/json`

## `slopmax login`

- **Usage:** `slopmax login [FLAGS] <PROVIDER>`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Connect an account: sign in, or enter an API key.

Subscriptions (claude, codex, grok) sign in through the provider's own page. API keys are asked for at a hidden prompt, or read from stdin (`slopmax login xai < key.txt`). A compatible endpoint needs --url.

### Arguments
- **`<PROVIDER>`** — Which kind of account

  **Choices:** `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, `anthropic`, `openai`, `xai`, `compat`

### Flags
- **`--label <LABEL>`** — Display name for the account (else its email)
- **`--device`** — Sign in with a code to enter on any device, instead of a browser redirect
- **`--no-browser`** — Print the sign-in address instead of opening a browser
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

### Compatible endpoints
- **`--url <URL>`** — The endpoint's base URL
- **`--dialect <DIALECT>`** — The API it speaks

  **Choices:** `chat`, `responses`, `messages`
- **`--models <MODELS>`** — Models it serves, as patterns (else what it lists)

### Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | it worked |
| `1` | it failed; the error says why |
| `2` | the command line was wrong |

### Examples

**Sign in to a Claude Pro or Max account**

```
slopmax login claude
```

**Sign in with a code, from a machine with no browser**

```
slopmax login codex --device
```

**Add a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint**

```
slopmax login compat --url http://localhost:11434/v1
```

## `slopmax account import`

- **Usage:** `slopmax account import [--adopt] [SOURCE]`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Copy the logins Claude Code, Codex, or CLIProxyAPI hold.

An imported login shares its refresh token with the tool it came from. CLIProxyAPI's are followed: slopmax reads the files CLIProxyAPI keeps fresh and never refreshes them itself, until `slopmax account adopt`.

### Arguments
- **`[SOURCE]`** — Where to import from

  **Choices:** `all`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `cliproxyapi`

  **Default:** `all`

### Flags
- **`--adopt`** — Refresh CLIProxyAPI's logins here instead of following its files
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

### Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | it worked |
| `1` | it failed; the error says why |
| `2` | the command line was wrong |

## `slopmax account redeem`

- **Usage:** `slopmax account redeem [-y --yes] <ACCOUNT>`
- **Effect:** destructive — may delete or irreversibly overwrite

Spend a banked limit reset, resetting the account's usage windows.

Claude and ChatGPT accounts can hold limit resets; this spends the one that expires soonest.

### Arguments
- **`<ACCOUNT>`** — A number from `slopmax status`, or the account's id, email, or label

### Flags
- **`-y --yes`** — Don't ask for confirmation
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

| `2` | the command line was wrong |

## `slopmax account adopt`

- **Usage:** `slopmax account adopt <ACCOUNT>`

  **Default:** `40`
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

### Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | it worked |
| `1` | it failed; the error says why |
| `2` | the command line was wrong |

## `slopmax config`

- **Usage:** `slopmax config [--json] [NAME] [VALUE]`
- **Effect:** modifies state

Show the routing settings, or change one while the proxy runs.

A change applies at once to a running proxy, and is saved to config.toml. The other settings live in config.toml itself.

### Arguments
- **`[NAME]`** — The setting, e.g. strategy
- **`[VALUE]`** — Its new value, e.g. round-robin

### Flags
- **`--json`** — Print JSON instead of text, for scripts and agents
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

### Output Formats

- **`human`** (default)

  **Framing:** `text`
- **`json`**

  **Framing:** `json`; **Select:** `--json`

  **Media type:** `application/json`

### Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | it worked |
| `1` | it failed; the error says why |
| `2` | the command line was wrong |

### Examples

**Take turns between accounts**

```
slopmax config strategy round-robin
```

Publish slopmax to your own machines with `tailscale serve`

- **`--port <PORT>`** — The port to serve on (else the proxy's)
- **`--user <LOGIN>`** — A tailnet login to let in without a key
- **`--admin <MACHINE>`** — A machine that may also manage slopmax
- **`--loopback`** — Serve the proxy's bare port, where every machine needs a key
- **`--socket`** — Serve the proxy's socket, which Tailscale lets only root publish
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

### Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | it worked |
| `1` | it failed; the error says why |
| `2` | the command line was wrong |

### Examples

**Let your own machines in without a key**

```
slopmax tailscale on --user you@github
```

## `slopmax completion`

- **Usage:** `slopmax completion [--install] [--force] <SHELL>`

Print or install a shell completion script

### Arguments
- **`<SHELL>`** — Shell to generate completions for

  **Choices:** `bash`, `elvish`, `fish`, `nu`, `nushell`, `powershell`, `pwsh`, `zsh`

### Flags
- **`--install`** — Write the script where the shell looks for it instead of printing it

  **Effect:** modifies state
- **`--force`** — With --install, replace a file that was not generated by usage

  The file is overwritten without a backup, which is why this is labeled destructive.

  **Effect:** destructive — may delete or irreversibly overwrite
- **`-h --help`** — Print help

### Exit Status

| Code | Meaning |
| ---- | ------- |
| `0` | it worked |
| `1` | it failed; the error says why |
| `2` | the command line was wrong |
